issue.title: Implement Conflict Detection for Offline Audio Takes
issue.body:
Fluent's current sync model does a blind overwrite: if two translators record the same pericope or verse while offline, whichever take syncs last silently replaces the other. This ticket introduces a version token on each recorded unit so the server can detect when an incoming take diverges from the current version and flag it as a conflict instead of overwriting. This is the foundational layer that all conflict resolution UI depends on.

NOTE TO DEVS: This is Claude's solution for handling conflict resolution. Please take this with a Claude sized grain of salt and toss it out if there are better ways to handle this. Not trying to overstep.

## Functional Requirements

### Version Token

- Assign a version token to each recorded unit (pericope or verse, depending on project configuration) on the server.
- Update the version token whenever a take is committed to the server for that unit.
- Include the unit's current version token in the sync payload sent to the client so the client knows what version it is recording against.

### Conflict Detection on Sync

- When a take syncs to the server, compare its base version token against the server's current version token for that unit.
- If the tokens differ, flag the unit as in conflict and store the incoming take alongside the existing one; do not overwrite.
- Support more than two conflicting takes per unit; do not cap how many takes can be in conflict simultaneously.

### False Conflict Suppression

- Before flagging a conflict, compare the content hash of the incoming take against all existing takes for that unit.
- If the incoming take's content hash matches an existing take, do not flag a conflict.

Note: Recording always happens at the sub-chapter level — pericope or verse depending on project configuration. Version tokens attach at that unit level only; chapter is a claiming and navigation unit, not a recording unit. See the Merge Conflict Resolution requirements for full context.

Note 2: The false conflict scenario is a sync retry, not two people independently recording identical audio (which is not realistically possible). A take can upload successfully but the client never receives confirmation due to a dropped connection, causing it to retry. On retry, the version token has already advanced from the first upload, which would incorrectly flag a conflict. The content hash check catches this and suppresses it.

### Eng note (updated)

Server work lives in **eten-tech-foundation/fluent-api#271** — don’t do/invent API work inside this mobile ticket by default.

**Preferred:** pull `fluent-api#271` into the same slice and ship mobile + API together as one feature (so we’re not mocking forever).

**Fallback:** if after a short spike the API side looks like a crazy amount of work, ship this ticket against mocks and leave `fluent-api#271` as the explicit follow-up. Call that out in the PR.

Don’t treat the Claude sketch in the description as gospel — use it as a starting point when pairing with the API ticket.
